claims.text: Premelting in HEA nanoparticles is primarily governed by surface segregation of elements with lower intrinsic melting points.
A segregated layer of lower-melting-point elements creates a thin liquid-like surface layer that catalyzes melting onset.
As-synthesized HEA nanoparticles can have near-homogeneous multicomponent distributions with minimal surface segregation.
Controlled post-synthesis annealing can promote surface segregation of lower-melting-point elements in HEA nanoparticles.
Compositional modification can enhance accumulation of lower-melting-point elements at nanoparticle surfaces.
The relevant structural mediator is enrichment of lower-melting-point elements in a segregated surface layer.
Annealing or compositional control promotes diffusion of lower-melting-point elements to the nanoparticle surface.
The enriched surface layer has a lower melting temperature than the bulk particle.
The enriched surface layer forms a liquid-like region well below the bulk melting point.
The liquid-like surface region destabilizes the remaining nanoparticle and triggers a cascade into complete melting.
Particles with induced surface segregation will premelt at a lower temperature than minimally segregated baseline particles.
Premelting onset can be detected as an endothermic DSC peak.
Premelting can be observed in situ as a liquid-like surface layer by TEM.
A baseline population with a relatively uniform elemental distribution and little segregation can be produced.
The proposed segregation effect should hold for HEA nanoparticles whose constituent elements have substantially different individual melting points.
The proposed effect should operate from approximately 0.8Tm to Tm.
The mechanism may not apply when the constituent elements have similar melting behavior.
Bulk defects, bulk diffusion, or grain-boundary effects may compete with or dominate the proposed surface-segregation mechanism.
A statistically significant reduction in premelting onset after verified surface enrichment would support the proposed mechanism.
Failure to observe a lower premelting onset in particles with verified induced segregation would falsify the hypothesis.
